title: Update is terrible
body: Why does the meal planner open on the first startup? I've selected a recipe, closed it, and when I open it again, it starts with the meal planner. Why doesn't it save or remember my settings?

title: Misleading
body: BE AWARE that if you purchase the Pro you cannot upload a picture of a recipe to keep unless you also purchase the monthly subscription. This is not made clear in the information describing the paid version.

title: Recipe import non-functional
body: I was so excited to purchase the plus version of this app and collect recipes that have been sitting around in hard copy. But I’m disappointed to see that the import function is completely non-functional now. Importing from camera just directs me to a page prompting me to purchase plus (which I already have) or the pricier plan, and there’s no way to actually do the import. I’ll be trying to get my money back.

title: Used to be 5 stars
body: Don’t offer a one-time purchase for all the Pro features only to lock some of those features behind a monthly description afterwards. Completely defeats the purpose of paying more upfront for a one time purchase. Scummy business practice.

title: You pay for it and then they change what you get
body: I paid for this app to get the ability to have unlimited recipes and to be able to import PDFs and take pictures of recipes to import them. It was great for the first couple months and then they made updates and now those features are behind a monthly fee. Talk about a bait and switch. The app is nice, I like the setup of it, and it is very user-friendly. I just feel like I got swindled out of money just to have features that I purchased for a lifetime taken away.

title: Could use help in the formatting department.
body: I’m OCD about the presentation and formatting of my recipes and that is falling apart in Crouton as it doesn’t seem to support tiered bulleted lists, etc. so I’m having to find creative workarounds. Additionally iCloud sync does not work. I added pictures to my recipes from my phone (since I used it to take the pics) and I’ve pushed sync on my iPhone and iPad more times than I can count and the pictures and both devices are still not in sync with each other. The solution offered in the app is turn off a bunch of the features you pay for with iCloud+? So many other apps have figured this out without this - reach out to other developers and ask for help (respectfully). Update: please fix annoying formatting issues like when you try to select text within the steps it wants to drag the whole back of text versus selecting - what kind of UI decision was that - imagine if every item you wanted to SELECT something Apple said no take the whole box and drag it - the more normal behavior is allowing people to select especially since you already have the sandwiches on the side to allow for re-ordering. Update 2: Smart Import is NOT smart. How do you take a numbered list and literally put ALL the steps for a whole section under one number - they’re literally numbered. There doesn’t seem to be a winner in this category of app - all have their own quirks and things that require you to fight the app versus the app just recording recipes as advertised - go figure. The Notes app is still the GOAT at this point. Update 3: another example of UI design and produces unintended changes: I realized I was editing part of a recipe that had already been editing and when to hit escape thinking it would take me back a screen. Apparently escape is programmed to discard all changes without any warning. So 30 minutes of work gone.

title: Awful experience
body: I installed Crouton on my MacBook M2 running Tahoe 26.5.1 and tried to manually enter a recipe. I first tried to give the recipe a name but I couldn’t type into that box. I thought, maybe there has to be an actually recipe before I can give it a name, so I typed in the ingredients and the steps and tried again. Still couldn’t type in the Recipe Name box. I tried saving it but couldn’t without giving it a name. This really looks like an IOS app that was ported to macOS without rigorous testing. I’ve uninstalled it.

title: Subscription required to import recipes
body: I’m on the plus version and I can’t import recipes from simple text files (markdown) or pdf’s unless I pay for a subscription. Pdf’s might be trickier but a markdown or text file, really? I understand subscriptions when there are server costs involved but for things that are easily processed on-device it’s just unacceptable, especially when a “plus” version has already been purchased.

title: Desktop app leaves much to be desired
body: - Can’t zoom recipe - no keyboard shortcuts - small windows for editing recipes just more cumbersome to use than iOS apps

title: Missing features
body: to the best of my knowledge, still no way to bulk delete recipes. When importing from another app, categories / folders do not sync.

title: Crouton: Recipe Manager
body: I love most parts of crouton. Now that I have quite a few recipes saved it lags quite a bit. The grocery list adds things separately instead of combining ingredients for the grocery list. And each ingredient that’s on the grocery list should also tell What recipe it’s coming from, if that makes any sense. 01.18.26 Just updated my iPad and the app won’t even open. I pad has iPadOS 26.2 on it. Also I’m not able to she crouton with anybody that doesn’t have an Apple device.

title: Unable to do basic functions without paying.
Let me rate recipes!
body: Please just give me the ability to rate recipes, mark recipies as “cooked” easily and mark recipies as “want to cook” easily 😭 then this app would be perfect I wish it would have the simplicity of the New York Times cooking recipie box. Where a recipe that’s been cooked, in your recipies list maybe has a green checkmark or something and you easily can select “cooked” from the top of your recipies. Automatically recipies are marked as cooked and maybe even log the times an dates when the recipies was cooked or cooked again so you can do stuff like see what you’ve cooked the most of when you’ve cooked something before and add ratings each time and maybe notes and tweaks

title: You can only have 5 recipes for free
body: Had this been known up front I wouldn’t have even bothered downloading and wasting my time. 5 recipes is pointless

title: How to get support
body: I have a plus subscription for this app but cannot use the camera to scan a recipe. The link to the support website has no contact information but nothing happens when I click the link; so here I am.

title: not good
body: I signed up for the monthly payment and the app works as if it is the free version which limits the amount of recipes I can have. It no longer allows me to download recipes from the web.

title: Limited Recipes in Free
body: You can only store 5 recipes unless you pay for more.

title: A cobbled mess
body: The app fails more than it functions. The developer Devin focuses on new flashy features instead of polishing the existing rough edges that are laden with bugs. To name just a few, the settings back button vanishes at will, recipes rarely add via URL, the groceries creates a new list in Reminders each time it syncs, recipe images go missing, and scaling a recipe struggles to recognize fractional measurements. Add to this the developer bleeds you with pricing separating critical functions into not one but TWO in-app purchases. I can't defend this app anymore.

title: Useless App
body: Totally most useless free version app.You only get 1 recipe for the free version and you need to get the subscription to see the other recipes. There isn’t even a trial to see if it works for you or not. This could have been a direct paid app instead of paying inside the app. The free version is just calendar with your meal plan which you can have it on your calendar.

title: Won’t refund
body: I purchased the “one time app purchase” which did not state that it wouldn’t have all features. I went to settings after noticing i didn’t have full “privileges” and realized you have to buy the annual subscription to get all features. I requested a refund for the original purchase (the full app one time purchase) and proceeded to purchase the annual plan. Well they’re refusing the refund me my original purchase claiming I don’t “qualify” for a refund. The annual subscription covers everything the one time app fee covers plus all the extras. So I feel very shafted. NOT happy and will not be continuing my service.

title: Features I purchased in the past now no longer available
body: I was happy to move to this app when I purchased this in the past. I was able to take photos of recipes and these would be smartly added via OCR. Was happy and decided to move from Paprika. However, tried to use the same feature only to find out that you now needed to pay extra (again!) via subscription. Felt like a bait and switch tactic. Please bring back the features we paid for, otherwise, might as well use Apple notes if that’s the case.

title: Only 5 recipes
body: For an app marketed as free on the App Store this app only allows you to add 5 recipes before telling you, you have to pay $20-30 dollars to be allowed to add more along with unlocking the rest of the features. While I understand unlocking extra features only allowing 5 recipes for the base is a little ridiculous I would understand 30-50 recipes seeing as they are our recipes we are adding but only 5 seems a stretch. Not to mention they don’t tell you the limit until you’ve reached it so I just spent over an hour entering in 4 recipes before realizing I have to pay to unlock the ability to add more. The app is great but the execution of level locking and transparency is poor.

title: Beautiful but pricey.
body: This app is absolutely beautiful. Unfortunately, being limited to 5 recipes without paying $25 to upgrade is very much a dealbreaker. I will be finding a new recipe app, sadly.

title: Has potential but no bulk import
body: This app is better thought through than many, but I already have ~100recipes saved in other platforms. I can export them as PDFs, but Crouton can only import 1 recipe at a time, and each one takes a minute or two to process... and you have to sit there and wait for it to finish each one. It would take many hours of tedious work to transition to it. Too bad, really. Many good ideas in the app.

title: Smart import
body: Should not be behind a subscription paywall. That should be the bread and butter for imports…on a recipe app….

title: Nice looks, pity about high pressure sales tactic.
body: I’m sure it’s a nice app, and they do a great job with staying current with Apple’s design ethos, but I hate, hate, HATE being pressured into decision-making such as Crouton’s offering a discount if I purchase the full version within the first 24 hours of downloading. Good apps can stand on their own merits. Also, importing recipes turned out to be more of a pain than I expected due to Crouton reading my “2-1/4” that I do for readability as “a range from two to one-fourth” rather than “two and one fourth”. Paprika may be showing its age, but at least it understands what I mean when I scale recipes without having to manually convert to “2¼”.

title: Great app except….
body: This is one of the best apps I’ve purchased. I love it! However, it used to sync between all my family members and no longer does. It used to be much better for this reason.

title: Bring your visa card
body: I don’t mind paying for apps but i wish they had said this app is worthless unless you pay our subscription fee. I was looking for a simple app to put a few recipes in for easy keeping. They have great tools for transferring from print to app but on the pay tiers. The manual entry was free but, unbeknownst to me, after a few it won’t let you do that anymore. I’d do better for my purposes on the Notes app I guess.

title: It has potential to be a great app
body: This is by far the most aesthetically pleasing recipe management app I've seen. It's super clean and has some great functionality like simple importing from websites, keeping the ingredients visible at all times when in a recipe, timer setting in the recipe step that calls for any amount of time, etc. I love all of those things. Some of the problems I've encountered are: - To add multiple tags to a recipe, you have to hold Command and click on the tags you want, which I've never seen on tag selection options in other apps - Along the same lines, when you select multiple recipes, you have to hold Command and click on them. Even though the interface brings up check boxes to the left of the recipes, they act like radio buttons, selecting only one object. If you click on another one, it deselects the last one. You shouldn't have to hold Command to select multiple recipes - You can't select multiple recipes when you do a search through all the recipes. It will pull up the recipes that match your search, but you can't select all of them and add a tag or batch move them to a folder. - If you try to use the Command F shortcut to search for recipes, there is no way to return to your list of all recipes. You just have to quit the app and open it back up again. - The iCloud syncing for families is pretty slow or doesn't work at all. My wife still has folders showing up in her account that I deleted months ago. I feel like these issues should be pretty simple to resolve, but they make the user experience absolutely miserable. I've taken it for granted that other apps and websites get things like this right, and this app just messes all of them up. If these issues are fixed, I'd be willing to change my rating to 5 stars

title: Used to be great
body: This used to be a great app and I used it all the time! Now it doesn’t pull recipes from websites correctly (e.g. if the recipe says “1 and 1/2 cups” it will only pull 1/2 cup). So now I can pretty much only use it as storage for links to recipes, not the recipes themselves, because I have to double check them all for errors. Great idea, poor usability, unfortunately.

title: Love the app… needs updates
body: I’m on my second year of paying for premium and while I truly love the app, there seem to be minimal to no improvements coming. For example, if the website has sections, it won’t read the sections. Additionally there is no way to “rate” recipes to help build a better meal plan for the week - in fact it doesn’t even de-dupe when creating a meal plan for the week. PLEASE FIX THESE BUGS and it’ll be a 5-star!

title: Was excellent but need to pay monthly for smart import loses stars
body: I loved this app and previously rated at five stars. It seems that overtime, they have taken some features and put it behind a monthly paywall. Specifically, smart import where you can get a PDF or text file and have it imported correctly into Crouton has now been moved behind a paywall. I already paid once, if I recall, about $20 for lifetime premium. Now it seems that this useful smart import feature is hidden behind a two dollar a month fee. I do not use this app regularly enough to warrant $24 per year for this Smart import feature. I will probably switch to a different app unfortunately

title: Apple Recipes
body: Can't import Apple recipes.

title: Good App Overall. Needs some improvements.
body: The app is good overall. The syncing is fast and accurate. The interface is good and usable. The cooking facial navigation is gimmicky and probably not usable for most unless you situate your device just right. We need spoken commands like next, back, ingredients, timer, etc. we all need a share extension to add recipes direct from the share menu rather than having to copy the URL and then navigate to the crouton app.

title: Groceries tab doesn’t import from recipes
body: Adding items to grocery list from a recipe does nothing

title: Not great for vision impaired
body: I wish the settings allowed me to change the font size.

title: I wanted to like it
body: Unfortunately, I have had to stop using the app and switched to a competitor because of a number of small but important issues for me. I have found that the app gets slow when having a large library and lacks some organization tools to make managing recipes easier. In addition, there are a large number of ui quirks that make use difficult as fixing them requires either switching to another section of the app and back or sometimes restarting the app altogether. I submitted these issues to the developer a few months ago, who essentially blew me off and said thanks for the feedback but he’s been too busy since winning the Apple design award and would consider fixing the issues if he has time. Since then, a number of new versions have been released, and only a single issue I reported was resolved. I also have a number of issues with recipe import. The biggest is support for sites that may be a little less known. When trying to import, I frequently have to manually import the picture, steps, and ingredients list even on sites that support the standard recipe schema. These issues make the share sheet fairly worthless for a lot of sites since you can’t copy and paste the missing data while that’s up. I have to either save the mostly blank recipe and go edit it or jump to the app and import there. The other thing I would prefer to see changed when importing pages is how the title is generated. Right now, it pulls the page title, which is often rewritten for SEO, and includes non-relevant data like the site name. I think it should use the recipe name from the page content instead. I know this isn’t perfect either, but it’s closer to correct more often than the page title. My last issue is the app says it can import recipes from Instagram. Unfortunately, I have yet to get it to work and always get back a blank recipe dialog with none of the fields filled out. Not sure if it’s just bad luck with the ones I’ve tried, but ultimately, I gave up on the feature.

title: Good, but could be so much better
body: I had to do a lot of editing in a recipe since the app misunderstood the scanned recipe, especially since my recipe had a separate crust section and its’ ingredients were thrown in with the main chicken pot pie ingredients.

title: Too expensive
body: The app is good but I don’t know why nobody is talking about how it’s $25 once you want to have more than 5 recipes. Paprika is the #1 paid app in this category and it’s exactly like this app but it’s $5. I switched over and love it.

title: Can't search recipe using my language
body: Even if I can create recipes using Chinese, I can't search using Chinese. Seems rediculous to me...

title: Good but a little buggy
body: It’s a good app but sometimes buggy and it doesn’t sync the grocery list with family sharing. The one other feature it needs is in the grocery section, when you put a checkmark ✅ by an item, it should move that item to the bottom so it’s out of the way. There’s an app called Grocery that does this and it would make this app much more useful. I hope that these features get worked out/added soon.

title: Seems nice, but no data portability
body: I can't find a way to import data from Paprika nor a way to export data out of Crouton. These apps try to lock you in, but what is a user to do when the developer no longer updates their software? And given my years-long investment in Paprika, I can't see starting all over even though this is much more Apple-like than Paprika and offers OCR for recipe scanning from books, which I sorely need. Worst case, I may have two sets of recipes for some time so I can finally get rid of all my recipe books. Definitely would recommend this over Paprika for people just starting out with digitizing recipes, though one thing I will say for Paprika is that I really like being able to organize my grocery list by aisle, since I only shop at one store and know the layout well enough that having Paprika organize my list by aisles speeds up my shopping tremendously. I can't see a similar feature in Crouton.

title: So tediuous
body: Not worth the money to upgrade. It doesn't make your cooking life any easier

title: It would be a good app….
body: If you could add more than five recipes on the free version. I wish this was stated from the beginning so I didn’t waste time adding and customizing recipes only to find out that this won’t be usable for me. I wanted to test this app as an alternative to my current practice of PDF’ing all my recipes to the Files app that’s neatly organized with folders. I don’t really understand the asking for tip if you’re going to paywall true functionality of the app. Overall, the features locked behind paywall aren’t worth it so that’s why recipe count is limited as well. It’s a shame because there was potential for this app and I would’ve supported via tip, but now it’s getting shelved in a folder for now and possibly deleted in near future.

title: Great
body: Really handy but lower the prices for premium

title: I LOVE THIS APP!!!
body: This app is AMAZING! It’s so amazing and I love that most of the features are free and the subscription is just $1.99 a month :) please never change that, I just have one thing I’d like to suggest, I’d love if the grocery list had pre generated things you could add or when you add a recipe for it to give you the option to paste those into your grocery list instantly, AMAZING app

title: Paprika-killer!
body: Thoroughly enjoy using this app, as I was a long time user of Paprika. My only suggestion would be to have synchronization for meal plans with Apple Calendar. I very much need that feature!

title: Great app! So handy, a little buggy.
body: I love this app. There are a few things that could be better though. Some recipes don’t import well and all the instructions are put into one step. If I use the share feature in Safari to share to Crouton, it sometimes freezes up and I have to quit Safari to get it working again.

title: Best recipe app
body: This is by far my favorite recipe app. My only issue is that there is still no integration with Google Calendar yet. It’s a pain to have to be going back and forth to schedule meals based on my school/work schedule. If Google cal integration was there, it would be unbeatable.

title: Great Recipe App
body: Crouton is a great recipe app. The interface is easy to use and I love that it is AI supported so It intuitively imports and creates recipes from text, links or downloads. I also like the sip by step cooking process where you click and it shows you the next step. I would give it 5 stars but at time it can be buggy and sometimes the imports can get ingredient quantities wrong. You also have to check to make sure they are correct. The other thing holding me back from a 5 star rating is that there is no Android app. Hello? 72% of people have Android phone as compared to 28% Mac. Extensions for Firefox and Chrome are also needed.

title: Paprika import
body: I really like the app. While Crouton does support importing a Paprika backup, the ability to import the Paprika folder structure would make like much easier. Having to sort my 1400 recipes to match Parila is quite daunting.

title: Could use one extra feature request AND A WEB APP PLEASE??
body: One feature I would love to see is a extra Siri Shortcut for ADDING GROCERIES. You have shortcuts action for recipes, meal plans, and step-by-steps. But it's missing one extra shortcut: ADD GROCERIES TO MY GROCERY LIST. Please add it. And PLEASE MAKE A WEB APP AND A WINDOWS APP. Not everyone who uses Crouton has a Mac. Even I don't have a Mac yet and would be years before getting to own one. At least add a Web App or make a Windows app for once!

title: Magically pulls recipes from web sites
body: First, let me say that Croutons is great. It’s like magic how you give it a URL and it will scrape a web page and create a recipe from it. I would rate it five stars if it had a way to annotate a recipe with additional notes. You can edit the recipe itself, but it would be nice to be able to include meta information that is specific to my kitchen or family (e.g., “use the top rack and increase the temp to 375 for better browning” or “too spicy for Jane so decrease cayenne to 1/2 tsp”).

title: Love it so much, with one exception
body: Everything about this is so well thought out. The timer, clicking on ingredients within the instructions, the meal planner, having folders plus tags available for sorting. I love it. The only thing I hate... And I mean *hate* …is when editing bulk ingredients or instructions if you pull down too hard it closes the window. I never know if I’m at the top of the recipe, so I pull too hard, and then I have to start all over. Sometimes I do this 3x in a row before thinking “just don’t try to look at the top. Save your work and then edit it after.” Otherwise it’s a 10/10 app.

title: Almost Perfect
body: I love the meal planning for the week, the ease to fill in recipes and import from website, & that it will automatically alert you to import from a site. The one issue for me is that sometimes when my screen goes dark or if I’m pulling from another app, it clears everything I have checked off on my grocery list. So I have to go back through and check what I already got so I don’t miss something. If that ever gets fixed, it will be a 5 star app for me.

title: Love this but…
body: Very easy to use. Love the add recipes from websites. Sadly it doesn’t work for all websites.

title: Nice UX but import tool not great unless you upgrade
body: Really love the attention to detail and thoughtful UX but found that the standard import tool for web recipes was really hit or miss - not great at all. But if you upgrade to the plan that includes the new AI import tool, I’ve found that much more reliable. It pulled in ingredients that the standard import missed - correctly separated steps in the recipe (instead of one big blob of text). I am hoping this sticks as I really like the app but the import functionality was holding me back from replacing other iOS recipe managers.

title: Cannot add more than 5 recipes
body: I bought the premium version but it keeps telling me that I cannot add anymore recipes. When I try to exit out the app crashes and I need to force quit. I now require to add the recipe via my phone, which is annoying.

title: Nearly the ultimate recipe app
body: This application is the one you’ve been looking for most likely. I’ve tried lots of different ones on the iOS platform and they all had pretty glaring shortcomings but this one nearly has it all and is so polished that I’m willing to look past it’s main issue. The nutrition field in a recipe is my only complaint, I wish I could input the macros for the dish (Calories, Protein, Fat, and Carbs) and it would dynamically show how much a serving would be. Currently the nutrition field is the same thing as writing a note, so if your making a smaller portion you have to do manual math each time. Other than that I love how you can tag meals, either with kitchen tools needed (Air Fryer, Electric Mixer etc) or if they are vegetarian, high protein etc. The organization is lovely too. If it wasn’t for the nutrition field feeling like an after thought it would be 5 stars to me.

title: Love the app but I wish I could send recipes to it via my PC
body: I really love how easy to use and customizable this app is. My partner is celiacs and vegan, and has allergies, and then I’m quite picky so we often alter recipes a lot! I love that I can change the recipes as much as I want and still have the link to the original one if my experimenting goes awry and I need to double check it. The only thing is I do tend to search for recipes while on breaks at work in my computer, and then I end up having to email them all to myself to then open up on my phone and painstakingly copy and paste them into the app. I wish there was a way to open the app on a browser to add the recipes. Other than that I love it.

title: I'm still learning
body: My computer skills are not stellar. I wish there were more resources for us newbies to find out how to do things.

title: Would Appreciate Shortcuts on macOS
body: I'm a Crouton Plus customer and I really appreciate the thorough library of shortcuts available on iOS. I'd really appreciate it if the same (or, at least the "Get Recipes for Date" action) was made available on macOS too so that the shortcuts I make could be used across platforms. Thanks!

title: The Best Recipe App I’ve Found!
body: This is the most efficient and cost-effective recipe app I have used. I have tried (& paid for) Paprika, Any List, Grocery, and SO many others. I went to each for the ease of a particular feature (or a few) and they always managed to either change/break the feature, have another feature that made the app frustrating to use, or require a subscription to be able to use it. Crouton beautifully imports recipes from 99% of the sites I get recipes from. It brings over most of the information I need. I really only need to manually put in what I want in the notes. The last app I used did not have scaling and it was SO FRUSTRATING. The fact that it can also AUTOMATICALLY convert standard to metric within the recipe and the hands free features are GAME CHANGERS! I love that it also has the option to show the ingredients you need at that particular step while looking at the instructions. And so many ways to sort-folders, tagging, smart folders (with more than one sort option!). For an app that is billed as a “hobby,” you can tell this is someone who cooks themselves and put so much thought into the app because they use it themselves. Thank you for this app!

title: Best Ever
body: The paid version of this app is so worth it. It can scan your recipes from your favorite cookbook into an easy to read recipe on your phone.

title: Better than ever other recipe app I’ve used!
body: What the title says! It’s so easy to use. And accurate website pastes/import FOR FREEEEE!!!

title: My Favorite App Hands Down
body: I use this to store recipes. No more scrolling life stories to get to the ingredient list. I use the Meal planner for the week, I add all the ingredients to my grocery list, cross off what is in my pantry already, and my grocery list is done! This has simplified my life and has helped me eat much healthier!

title: Must Have!
body: This app is beautifully built, practical, functional, and thoughtful. It is an app my wife and I use every day. It is so practical for meal planning, quickly accessing recipes, and meal prepping. The way that it is designed for all devices with iCloud sync is brilliant! This functionality makes it easy to meal prep with my wife and see recipes on multiple devices. Lastly, the AI quick add recipe features make it SO easy to add new recipes to our library and share them with friends/family (the subscription is worth it!). Couldn’t recommend this app enough!

title: Affordable and Easy to use
body: I have had this amazing app for over a year now. I recently started canning and preserving my food again and this app has made it so easy to keep recipes that I want to try. Whether it be regular dinners or canning/preserving recipes I have it all at my fingertips because of this app! Please note though: I do still keep hard copy books because it is still technology and there is always a chance that this will go down at some point!

title: Excellent Recipe Manager
body: I’m obsessed with converting recipes I find on Instagram, blogs, and even cookbooks into meal plans for the week. The cost for Plus/Discover is a fraction of the cost of competitors and it syncs smoothly to other household members and the kitchen iPad for cooking. Love it.

title: Perfect but a few features I’d like to request
body: Please add the ability rate a recipe and it show visually as you look through recipes. I have a lot of recipes and it really helps if I can see which ones I’ve made and rated highly. Also I wish we could toggle between or have added a meal planner queue. I don’t always have recipes planned for a certain day depending on left overs or appetite. It’s nicer for me to have a Queue of recipes to reference that I’d like to try making soon or next.

title: Really incredible app
body: I love this app so so so so much, and I love the updates it has received over the years. It easily scrapes websites for recipes and saves them to your local device, and it’s gotten better with time. I have nothing but the highest praise for this app!!!

title: Day One Paprika defected to this gem…
body: Look no further, this multi OS app is the best. I used Paprika from day one. But the development team seemed to be happy no evolving, and also not taking my repeated suggestions to incorporate OCR/AI supported importing from camera. It’s a game changer. I’m at someone”s house, they have that killer recipe in a cookbook, and in less than 10 seconds, it’s perfectly imported into Crouton. And by the way, if you used to use Paprika, one can import your full data set into Crouton.

title: The best recipe APP EVER!!!
body: Whoever came up with this app is a genius. This app is simple but gives you so much. I love the meal plan and grocery shopping linked to my Apple Notes grocery list which I share with my husband. Might try the discover features. Yes, it is worth the price, I promise because I don’t like in-app purchases!

title: New User
body: I have been wanting to digitize my recipes and after some research landed on Crouton as a solution. So far, so good. Looking forward to fully utilizing its functionality and handoff feature between my laptop for entry and iPhone for accessing ingredients when I grocery shop.

title: Easy way to keep up with your recipes

title: Game Changing Recipe Manager
body: This app has been a game changer for our family. We struggle with keeping track with the recipes we like, knowing which ingredients to buy and update, and which nights of the week we feel motivated to actually cook. We started to default to a few basic and routine meals that meant dining out was an easy out. This app has changed the game. - We already utilized the Reminder app on iOS to share a family grocery shopping list. This continuity was great and having the ability to cross between apps is amazing. Especially when we can shop for the recipes! - the meal planner is a major upgrade from using a shared calendar event. This allows us to choose or have a random recipe chosen and then the decision is made. No more last minute “lets just go out to eat instead” because we bought the ingredients, know its a meal we chose and we love. - The AI Import for recipes is amazing. We have so many recipes typed out in the notes app, saved on instagram, in physical cook books (including my grandmothers 1950 recipes that I care so much about). We spent a day just taking pictures from books - start with the picture of the food picture if it has it, and then the AI takes wildly typed recipes and makes it a simple format to utilize. - I can probably type 4-5 more great thoughts on this app and I cant wait for the companion thermometer from Combustion Inc. to arrive. This app makes me want to cook again and not just default to eating out.

title: What an App should be!
body: This app deserves 10 stars. The UI is pleasing to look at and intuitive to navigate. It is easy to add and edit recipes. The accuracy of import is almost always spot on. Recipe mode makes it SUPER easy to follow your recipe... and the added "wink left / wink right" to move to the next step is AWESOME (because everyone knows, while you're cooking, your hands end up covered in food that you don't want on your screens!). The developer(s?) have taken great care to make this app the best it can be. They've even responded to a feedback suggestion I submitted for improving the grocery list section! Well done y'all!

title: The best recipe app with NO subscription!!
body: I almost never review apps, but Crouton is special. This is as independent-developer as apps get: it's just one guy. He saw a gap, figured out how to fill it, and single-handedly delivered a solution. Pretty incredible. But cool story aside, the app itself is fantastic! It's full of great features to facilitate easy organization and accessibility, like tag-based smart folders, a "play" mode for viewing recipes in step-by-step fullscreen, different options for color-coding steps — I love the "rainbow" setting, the randomly-assorted colors make reading/tracking through a recipe much easier on my brain — and a grocery list that auto-syncs with the Reminders iOS app. It's cute yet functional, simple yet robust, and overall very impressive. But in the end, what made me choose Crouton over the dozens of other apps on the market: IT'S NOT A SUBSCRIPTION!! In this capitalist nightmare — where companies force you to rent the products & services that facilitate the most basic facets of your life for upwards of $10/month a piece — this is an app you can still actually *buy*, once, and then you just own it? Forever? You don't have to ongoingly lease your own recipes?? Crazy concept, I know. But it's that kind of business integrity that made this app the unequivocal winner in my book. Keep doin' what you're doin', Devin! You're the best!

Other great features let us organize recipes into folders, print or email them as PDFs, add photos and notes, and search keywords (including ingredients, not just recipe titles). We don't use our "recipe box" for grocery shopping, so I can't say how well that component functions. But Crouton is PERFECT for our needs, works great and we love using it. I also appreciate that it's developed by an independent programmer who over time continues to tinker with adding new features and improvements. I've recommended Crouton to several other people who also tell me they are glad to have found it! It's absolutel one of most-used apps, I probably open it every day......Thanks Crouton!

title: “The One”
body: Rarely do I leave app reviews, but Crouton made the exception list. I have tested just about every recipe manager app there is; I used Paprika for years, tried Pestle, gave a few of the others a shot, etc. When I discovered Crouton it blew all of the others out of the water. From the native iOS look and feel, to the customization and support, this app has it all. The developer is also extremely responsive and passionate about his app, which is a huge factor when comparing apps that have similar functionality. So, if you’re like me and have been searching through all of the recipe management apps out there looking for “the one”, I highly recommending giving this one a shot, you won’t be disappointed!

I had so many recipe apps before this one and they all ticked some but not all boxes. This one ticks all! Purchased the upgrade without hesitation. The developer clearly put thought and intention into this design and it shows! Also deeply appreciate the affordability. It is so refreshing to be able to buy a digital asset with a one-time fee.
